boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Tampa record (June 30-July 1, 1862) in Operations Against Tampa [June-July 1862]. Campaign-wide marches, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads one gunboat (US) and a company of Osceola Rangers (CS); the live field reads zero. Pearson says the gunboat sent a launch with a lieutenant and 20 men, that he met it with 18 men in one of his boats, and that his batteries consisted of three 24-pounder cannon, one manned by a green squad under Captain Gettis. Finegan, reporting from Tallahassee, says two companies, Pearson's and Chambers's, were stationed at Tampa and that the enemy force was one vessel.
claims.rationale: Unit and gun counts from two Confederate reports; no Union report was found (see open questions). One company (frozen) against two (Finegan) is preserved. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Finegan's report rests on advices that the batteries were replying and says he apprehended no attempt to capture Tampa; Pearson relies on onlookers for the claim that the vessel was struck and says he cannot tell what damage was done.
claims.rationale: Secondhand knowledge in both reports. No original reconnaissance, order or message chain was inspected to establish contemporary knowledge. Surprise in a summary does not independently establish what each commander knew. Finegan's report is dated July 8 but speaks of the firing in the present tense.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Confederate victory (Inconclusive, but Union gunboat withdrew.); the live result reads Confederate Victory. Pearson says the firing ran about an hour from 6 p.m. on June 30 and two hours on July 1, after which the vessel weighed anchor and left the town in Confederate possession; NPS says the gunboat withdrew in the afternoon of July 1.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The frozen text's own qualifier (inconclusive) is preserved.

open_questions: No Union account was found: the targeted follow-up searched Official Records of the Navies I, 17 (East Gulf Blockading Squadron) and found no report of the June 30-July 1, 1862 bombardment. Drake's report, if any, and the vessel's log remain unlocated.
Chambers's company and the Tampa garrison return remain uninspected.

NPS/CWSAC (NPS battle page and frozen Arnold rows) is one family. J. W. Pearson's July 2, 1862 report and Joseph Finegan's July 8 report (Official Records I, XIV) are interested Confederate accounts; Finegan wrote from Tallahassee on advices. No history covering this action was found; two report families plus NPS are recorded as the effort ceiling. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
